provenance.extraction_invocation: uv run python -m code_extension.slice --scenario worker-start-budget --oakridge <oakridge> (git show 1495ec34d63a3147c60203ec7877cc2667212e93:<path> for each file the scenario's module in code_extension/library/ lists)
extraction_rules: Ship the pinned import closure of the files the feature passes through, and the pinned tests that exercise them.
Keep hidden checks, patches and qualification assets outside repository/.
licenses: Oakridge is private source at the pinned commit; no standalone license file is present.
The locked third-party packages carry their notices in package-lock.json.
local_adaptations: Only relative import paths change, as each file moves; the slice spec lists every edit.
Test helpers that would open Postgres or the Rust core are replaced by the one function the shipped tests use.
The slice is worker-silence-bound's, unchanged but for the package name, so this control's start tree matches that task's; its provider test stays in the hidden regression group there and here.

public_requirements: A worker's launch settings may include deadline_ms, a positive integer number of milliseconds, and max_start_attempts, a positive integer; the effect instruction built for that agent worker carries them instead of the defaults.
A budget field that is not set keeps its default, and a worker without a budget keeps both defaults, even when another worker in its stage sets one.
A deadline_ms or max_start_attempts that is not a positive integer makes the configuration malformed; harness and model stay required.
An unset budget adds no key to parsed configurations or to the instruction's worker settings.
